To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed and implemented a system, Olympian that enables TF Serving to run multiple DNN models on a shared GPU in a fair and low overhead fashion.

we have designed and built a GPU scheduling system, Olympian that can achieve fair sharing of the GPU across concurrent DNNs with an overhead of less 2%, and that can achieve differentiated service for DNNs.

(1) we can achieve fair sharing of a single GPU between concurrent large DNN models at low overhead, and (2) the key to doing this is to profile DNN resource usage and use the profiles to schedule DNNs at timescales of milliseconds.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the problem of how to fairly share the GPU across multiple large DNN models in TF Serving, and our solution, Olympian, achieves this by using a novel approach that leverages the predictability of GPUs to achieve low overhead DNN scheduling.
how to schedule and account for the usage of DNNs in the context of a DNN-serving system.
scheduling DNNs in serving systems to achieve service differentiation objectives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Olympian is the first system to provide fair sharing of a single GPU across concurrent DNNs.
Olympian provides a fair share scheduler for DNN models running in a serving system that can run multiple DNNs concurrently on a single GPU with minimal overhead.

our work provides an important capability for TF Serving and cloud based DNN serving systems, and is an enabler for a wide range of applications, including fairness and differentiation in cloud based DNN offerings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are the first to address the problem of scheduling DNNs for fair usage on a single GPU in a serving system.
, Olympian is a fair and low overhead scheduling system for concurrent large DNN inference jobs on a GPU, which is crucial for cloud based TF Serving.
we present the problem of scheduling concurrent DNNs on a GPU, present a solution, and evaluate it in a TF Serving system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by leveraging GPU predictability, it is possible to schedule DNNs at fine timescales, with low overhead, while accounting for their usage.
it is possible to achieve fair sharing of GPUs across multiple DNNs at a very low cost, and that the predictability of GPUs makes this feasible.
it is possible to schedule concurrent DNNs with low overhead and high fairness, a crucial capability for cloud offerings.
